lines.text: good? In order to understand this we must remember that
what is in view here is not any worldly or political issue but
the ultimate issue, that of eternity, that of God. And here in
the decisive question of God it is always better to decide
against God than to be poised indecisively in a middle
term. For the struggle against God implies always a certain
degree of connexion with God; every struggle against God
is a wrestling with God, as the example of one of the most
passionate fighters against God, Friedrich Nietzsche, can
show.
It must of course be a genuine and honest struggle against
God. A struggle which understands the question of God only
in theoretical terms or only as a political issue is not that.
Such an attitude is in fact an ignoring, a silencing of the
profound and searching question of the reality of God. And
such a fighter is the half-hearted indecisive person for whom
the question of the reality of God in all its seriousness and
depth has not yet become vivid. But the passionate fighter
against God stands near to God and his ear is open to the
voice of eternity. Mere talk about God and religious belief
does not of course bring us near to the living majesty of
God. A man may talk a great deal about God and yet
belong to the category of these half-hearted persons; for the
search for God is only genuine when it stirs and masters
man's mind as a passionate concern. Are we the kind of
men for whom the question of God is a passionate concern?
Or have we squandered our inner strength on other
questions?
"Behold, I stand at the door and knock." How will it be
when the Eternal opens the door? Whom will He find?
Alas, the most terrible thing of all is not that He should find a
foe in our breast, but if He finds no one there, if our souls
are hollow and void! For the most frightful danger we incur
is that we lose our souls in preoccupation with our duties and
cares, our joys and sorrows, and that in our innermost selves
we cease to be anything that has meaning; if in this situation
eternity knocks at our door, it will find no one there! This dan-
